newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco Ltd confirms tentative Sudbury deal.
newsitem.headline: Inco Ltd confirms tentative Sudbury deal.

text.p: Canadian nickel giant Inco Ltd confirmed on Friday that it reached a tentative agreement on a new three-year contract with unionized workers at its Ontario division.

"We are pleased that the bargaining committee for the United Steelworkers of America Locals 6500 in Sudbury and 6200 in Port Colborne has decided to unanimously recommend this new contract offer to its membership," Jim Ashcroft, president of Inco's Ontario division, said in a statement.
To allow time for a vote on the deal, Inco and the union have extended the current contract deadline until midnight Monday, June 2.
The union had set a strike deadline for midnight Saturday.
Inco said the union had scheduled information meetings for its members today.

"The next three years represent a major challenge for the Ontario Division and a new collective bargaining agreement will allow us to move forward in meeting this challenge by working together to improve productivity and efficiency," Ashcroft said.
Union members had voted 98 percent in favor of giving union leaders the mandate to strike if a tentative agreement could not be reached by May 31.
The contract affects about 4800 workers at the nickel giant's mining, smelting and refinery operations in Sudbury and its refinery in Port Colborne.

According to Inco's production plan for the current fiscal year, the Ontario division is expected to produce about 230 million pounds of nickel, about 200 million pounds of copper, and about four million pounds of cobalt.
